questions.question: Three vertices of a square are A(3, 3), B(-3, 3) and C(-3, -3). Plot these and find the coordinates of the fourth vertex D and its area.
solutionSteps: Plot A(3,3) in I, B(-3,3) in II, C(-3,-3) in III.
AB is horizontal (length 6). BC is vertical (length 6).
D must be 6 units right of C or 6 units below A.
Coordinates: x=3, y=-3. So D is (3, -3).
Side of square = 6 units. Area = 6 × 6 = 36 sq units.

questions.question: Plot the points P(-2, 1), Q(2, 1), R(2, -1) and S(-2, -1). Name the figure formed and calculate its perimeter.
solutionSteps: Since opposite sides are equal and it's aligned with axes, it is a rectangle.

questions.question: A rectangle has length 8 units and breadth 5 units. One vertex is at (2, 1). If the sides are parallel to the axes and the rectangle lies in the first quadrant, find the coordinates of the other three vertices.
solutionSteps: All x and y are positive, so it stays in I quadrant.

questions.question: Show that the points (2, 0), (-2, 0) and (0, 2) are vertices of an isosceles triangle.
solutionSteps: Since AC = BC, the triangle is isosceles.

questions.question: Calculate the area of the triangle formed by joining the points (0, 0), (4, 0) and (0, 3).
solutionSteps: The vertices are at the origin, 4 units on x-axis, and 3 units on y-axis.
This forms a right-angled triangle with base = 4 and height = 3.
